headline: High-risk shared-workspace and MCP pairing: Windsurf can read/write local files while MinerU exposes document-processing outputs, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes an MCP server and processes untrusted PDFs/OCR text; Windsurf also uses MCP servers and can ingest workspace/clipboard content. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if MinerU outputs are copied or routed into Windsurf without provenance checks. The shared channel is not explicit, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty escalation.
conditions: IF MinerU output is pasted into Windsurf prompts or files
IF either MCP server forwards raw document text without provenance tags
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the tools
Route MinerU output through a plain-text sanitizer
Add provenance labels to all imported snippets
Review MCP server allowlists before enabling them
Use separate workspaces for extraction and coding

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, images, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, JSON, and OCR text, while Windsurf reads workspace files and can write them back. If sensitive documents are processed by MinerU and then opened in Windsurf in the same workspace, leakage can occur through editor context, logs, or model-proxy uploads. The shared filesystem path is documented on Windsurf, so medium fits.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are stored in the same workspace Windsurf opens
IF Windsurf sends open-file contents to its model proxy during assistance
mitigations: Keep MinerU inputs in a separate directory
Open only redacted copies in Windsurf
Turn off auto-sync for the shared workspace
Restrict Windsurf to a minimal project folder
Delete extracted intermediates after review

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU is read-only on filesystem but does use MCP and concurrent inference; Windsurf has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification plus shared state via local filesystem. In a shared workspace, Windsurf can overwrite or race with MinerU-produced artifacts, and the pair lacks documented locking. Because the write side is broad and defaults are dangerous, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory
IF Windsurf auto-executes edits while MinerU is still producing outputs
mitigations: Use separate output and source directories
Pause Windsurf before running MinerU jobs
Commit or snapshot files before agent handoff
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU generates extracted text, tables, and OCR artifacts that Windsurf can treat as input for code changes or commands. Windsurf’s agentic loop and command execution mean unverified extraction errors can cascade into incorrect edits or actions. Since no verification step is documented between them, the default interaction is unsafe enough for high severity.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses MinerU output as authoritative context
IF extracted OCR or table data is used to generate code or commands
mitigations: Require human review before acting on MinerU output
Compare extracted text against the source document
Use a checksum or diff step between tools
Disable command auto-run in Windsurf
Limit MinerU output to review-only artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as private and fully offline, while Windsurf is a closed-source editor with broad network egress and model-proxy use. The main compliance issue is a residency/retention mismatch if regulated documents are moved from offline extraction into Windsurf’s cloud-connected workflow. This is lower than medium because no specific regulated data class is stated.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-bound documents are opened in Windsurf
IF Windsurf uploads open-file context to a third-party model proxy
mitigations: Keep regulated documents only in MinerU
Use local-only or offline mode in Windsurf
Redact personal data before handoff
Review vendor retention settings
Obtain a DPA before processing EU data
